Proposes an approach; secondary: Evaluates — file-based cross-interface persistent-memory system (MEMORY.md + CLAUDE.md per project, synchronised between a web chat and a local coding agent), with a single-user proof-of-concept functional demonstration (n = 1)

Authors' cross-interface persistent-memory system (unnamed; no version), built on Created.app/Supabase web app, self-hosted n8n v1.121.0, Claude API (claude-sonnet-4, not pinned), GitHub, Obsidian + Obsidian Git plugin, Claude Code MCP plugin; extends Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern (April 2026 Gist)

Per project, two Markdown files in a Git-versioned Obsidian vault: MEMORY.md (Session + Project Memory: six fields summary, decisions, pending tasks, artifacts, errors, continuation point; append-only) and CLAUDE.md (Technical Memory: architecture, APIs, code decisions; append-with-timestamp, revised policy). Not specifications

(1) User copies a web conversation into the web app and submits it; (2) n8n webhook, JavaScript preprocessing, Claude API extracts six-field JSON; (3) primary pathway updates session status and appends to MEMORY.md via GitHub Contents API (fallback: raw text to Google Drive); (4) Obsidian Git pulls every 5 min; (5) local coding agent (Claude Code) reads MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md on launch; (6) user types /done at end of a coding session to update CLAUDE.md

None implemented. User-triggered steps only (submit conversation; /done). A human verification gate (user confirms extracted decisions/tasks) is recommended for clinically adjacent use but not implemented; Git history as audit trail
Full workflow of the proposed memory pipeline, run once end-to-end (single artefacts: context/memory files MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md read by the coding agent)
Not classifiable (persistent context/memory files for a coding agent, no specification); authors use no SDD terms ("persistent memory", "integration pattern")
